evidence: Ov. F. 5.501: longa via est, nec tempora longa supersunt
Hor. S. 1.5.104: Brundisium longae fīnis chartaeque viaeque est
terms.comment: Of the distance still to go, or already gone. Where English “a long way” only says how far off a thing is, Latin uses the adverb: longē abest (see far).

terms.gloss: a long journey, a long way
evidence: Sen. Ep. 6.5: longum iter est per praecepta, breve et efficāx per exempla

terms.comment: Seneca sets the long road and the short side by side. Of the little left to go, Brevis est via (see it won’t be long); as an adverb, “a short way” is paulum: paulum prōgressī.

phrases.latin: Longa via est ad avōs; dormī paulisper in autoraedā.
phrases.english: It’s a long way to Grandma and Grandpa’s; have a little sleep in the car.
We’ll go a short way further and then sit down.

phrases.latin: longa via est, nec tempora longa supersunt
phrases.english: it’s a long way, and there isn’t much time left

phrases.latin: Brundisium longae fīnis chartaeque viaeque est.
phrases.english: Brundisium is the end of a long story and a long road.
